title: Paths to Causality: Finding Informative Subgraphs Within Knowledge Graphs for Knowledge-Based Causal Discovery

problem.claim: Inferring causal relationships between variable pairs is important for understanding multivariate interactions in complex systems.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based methods for knowledge-based causal discovery often produce unstable and inconsistent results, compromising their reliability for causal inference.

contributions.claim: A knowledge-based causal discovery approach integrates Knowledge Graphs with Large Language Models.
The approach identifies informative metapath-based subgraphs in Knowledge Graphs and refines their selection with Learning-to-Rank models.
The selected top-ranked subgraphs are incorporated into zero-shot prompts for LLM-based causal relationship inference.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce a novel approach that integrates Knowledge Graphs with Large Language Models for knowledge-based causal discovery.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on biomedical and open-domain datasets report that the method outperforms most baselines by up to 44.4 F1 points across diverse LLMs and Knowledge Graphs.
The authors report that their code and datasets are available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Causal relationship inference is important for understanding multivariate interactions in complex systems.
Knowledge-based causal discovery offers an alternative to observational-data-based methods by reasoning over variable metadata.
LLM-based approaches can be unstable and inconsistent, limiting their reliability.
The proposed method selects and ranks informative Knowledge Graph subgraphs before incorporating them into zero-shot LLM prompts.
The authors report improved F1 performance over most baselines and public availability of code and datasets.

source_observation.claim: Selecting informative metapath-based Knowledge Graph subgraphs and refining the selection with Learning-to-Rank models is followed by improved reported causal inference performance.

interpretation.claim: Targeted retrieval of structured contextual evidence may help make LLM-based causal inference more effective and consistent.

application.claim: For knowledge-based inference tasks, retrieve and rank task-relevant subgraphs before supplying them to an LLM.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy improves performance for domains, models, or graph types beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the biomedical and open-domain datasets.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated LLMs, Knowledge Graphs, or baselines.
The abstract does not clarify whether the reported 44.4-point improvement applies uniformly across settings or to a particular evaluation.
The abstract does not describe the Learning-to-Rank models or the metapath-selection criteria.
